chunks: Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There is no journey that reaches deeper into the flesh, nor blood, nor skin, nor hair, than the journey to Mecca; and no one reaches it until hardship befalls him.
ai.seo_question: What makes the journey to Mecca physically more demanding than other travels according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) describes the journey to Mecca for Hajj as the most physically demanding pilgrimage, causing hardship that permeates the entire body—flesh, blood, skin, and hair. This narration highlights the spiritual and physical purification achieved through the endurance of travel difficulties. In Shia tradition, this 'travel' (safar) is often interpreted not merely as geographical distance but as the arduous spiritual ascent (suluk) required to attain proximity to God, where the physical strain serves as a means of expiating sins and refining the soul.
